note: Situation Reaction Test practice sets. Situations rewritten for this app from themes widely published in SSB preparation material. Practice prompts only - not official board papers.

sets.name: Situation Set 1 — Action and Duty
situations: He is cycling to his board examination when his chain snaps two kilometres from the centre.
She finds a wallet stuffed with cash and an identity card on a park bench.
As the trek leader, he realises the group has lost the trail as darkness falls.
He is on night duty at a forward post when he hears movement along the fence.
Her younger brother's school fee is due tomorrow and there is very little money at home.
He wakes at midnight to the smell of smoke coming from the flat above his.
Two days before the deadline, his project team stops replying to messages.
He reaches an accident site first and finds the rider bleeding and unconscious.
She is posted at a remote border post and the radio has been silent for six hours.
His motorcycle runs out of fuel on an empty highway at night.
He notices a classmate copying answers during the final examination.
A stranger collapses in a crowded railway compartment.
She is appointed captain of the college team and two seniors openly oppose it.
He loses the suitcase containing his certificates on the way to the SSB centre.
While boating, he sees a boy being pulled away by the current.
He is asked for a bribe by a clerk to release his passport.
His mother is unwell and he is the only one at home.
He is leading a group project in which nobody is willing to work.
She sees a man snatching a woman's chain in a crowded market.
He finds his hostel roommate unconscious after complaining of chest pain.
His flight is delayed and he will certainly miss an important interview.
He is caught in heavy rain with an important file he must keep dry.
He sees a group of men teasing a girl at a bus stop.
He is asked to speak at a function in front of a large audience.
His friend asks him to help cheat in an examination.
He is the only person present when a gas cylinder catches fire in the kitchen.
He loses his way while driving through an unfamiliar town at night.
A small child is found crying alone at a fairground.
He is told his leave has been cancelled on the day of his sister's wedding.
He sees a speeding truck hit a cyclist on the highway.
He must submit a report by morning but the electricity has gone out.
His teammate is injured minutes before an important match.
He finds a live electric wire lying on a flooded street.
He is asked to lead a rescue team although he has no such experience.
He witnesses a colleague being blamed for a mistake he did not make.
His wallet and telephone are stolen in an unfamiliar city.
He is travelling by train when armed men enter the compartment.
A friend borrows money from him repeatedly and never returns it.
He realises he has boarded the wrong train as the ticket checker arrives.
He finds a boy drowning in the village pond while walking home.
His bicycle tyre is punctured while he is rushing to an interview.
He is elected group leader but the group refuses to follow his plan.
He sees a woman being robbed just as the train starts to move.
An epidemic breaks out in the village where he is posted.
He must reach the examination centre during a citywide transport strike.
He is the first to notice a small fire in the office records room.
He is asked to organise a farewell for a teacher he does not like.
His parents want him to marry someone he has not chosen.
He is learning to sail when the boat's steering fails in rough water.
He is scolded by his supervisor in front of the whole team for something minor.
He needs an urgent operation but has nobody to look after him.
A bridge on his route has been washed away and the group must cross before dark.
He notices that his closest friend has stopped attending classes.
He is alone in the jungle at night during a trek when he hears footsteps.
He is asked to deliver cash along a route where robberies are common.
His boat capsizes while crossing a flooded stream.
He sees a man being electrocuted while working on a pole.
He is on a picnic when two of his friends begin a heated argument.
He finds his friend about to jump from a bridge.
He discovers that a question paper he is carrying has leaked before the examination.

sets.name: Situation Set 2 — Pressure and Judgement
situations: He is riding home when he runs over a stray dog.
She discovers her mobile telephone is missing just after leaving the metro.
His admit card cannot be found on the morning of the final examination.
As basketball captain, he finds his best player injured before the final.
He sees three men following him on a deserted road at night.
His team is far behind its target with only one week left.
He finds a thief jumping out of his window at midnight.
He feels his seniors are treating him unfairly.
He hears a child crying from inside a locked car on a hot afternoon.
He is selected for a prestigious course that clashes with his brother's wedding.
He sees a purse snatcher grab a bag on a moving train.
He has to complete a critical assignment while his father is in hospital.
His close friend is spreading false stories about him.
He is asked to apologise for something he did not do.
He arrives at a village to find its only hand pump has broken down.
He is leading a camping group that has lost its way.
A senior asks him to falsify a report.
He is told that his name has been left off the final selection list.
He sees a passenger fall from a moving train.
He is stuck in a lift with two strangers during a power cut.
He must arrange a blood donor urgently for an accident victim.
His younger sister tells him she is being bullied at school.
He is asked to volunteer for a task far below his ability.
He is on a hike when a teammate sprains his ankle badly.
He has to cross a river in spate to reach the village clinic.
He is asked to lead a group of people much older than himself.
He finds his bank account has been debited for a purchase he never made.
He is caught riding without a helmet by the traffic police.
He sees a friend's answer sheet being swapped by an invigilator.
He is in charge of a camp where the food supplies have run short.
He is asked to give a speech at a function he does not support.
He finds his roommate has taken his books without asking.
His vehicle breaks down while he is escorting a patient to hospital.
He witnesses a hit-and-run accident while waiting at a bus stop.
He is offered a job that pays well but requires him to live far from his family.
He finds that a junior is being ragged by seniors.
He is posted in a flood-hit area and must move people to safety.
He sees smoke rising from a building he has just left.
He is asked to accompany a stranger on a night journey.
He is informed that his best friend has met with an accident.
He realises the train he is on has caught fire in a rear coach.
He must decide between continuing his studies and supporting his family.
He is asked to organise a cultural event with no budget at all.
He sees two groups about to clash during a festival.
He is on his first solo flight when the weather turns bad.
He notices that a colleague has been drinking before coming on duty.
He finds a packet of narcotics hidden in the bus he is travelling in.
He is stranded in a hill station after a landslide blocks the road.
He is asked to referee a match between the teams of his two closest friends.
He wakes up to find his hostel on fire.
He is asked to raise money for a charity in a very short time.
He sees an elderly man struggling with heavy luggage on a staircase.
He discovers his project partner has copied work from the internet.
He is delayed by a crowd blocking the road on his way to an examination.
A snake is found in the room where he is staying with small children.
He is blamed for damage he did not cause.
He is asked to share a stage with someone who has publicly insulted him.
He has to stop his friend from driving after drinking.
He is the only one who can read the map during a trek in thick fog.
He receives a telephone call informing him that his unit is being mobilised immediately.

sets.name: Situation Set 3 — Nerve and Loyalty
situations: He is on the way to his interview when his vehicle meets with an accident.
He sees a crowd chasing a man they claim is a thief.
He is asked to guard a prisoner who turns out to be a relative.
He has to write an examination the day after his mother's operation.
He finds that the water in the village well has been poisoned.
He is leading a patrol when he loses radio contact with base.
He is asked to tell the truth against a senior officer.
A boy falls into an open manhole in a crowded street.
He is travelling by train when his reserved seat is taken by a frail senior citizen.
He has to choose between two friends who each ask him to take sides.
He is asked to donate blood during an emergency although he is weak.
He finds a colleague asleep on duty at a critical post.
He is asked to hand over confidential papers without authority.
He is on leave when he is recalled for an emergency.
He sees a school bus stuck in a flooded street.
He is asked to lead when he feels another person is more capable.
He is offered a promotion that his juniors deserve more.
He is stranded on a railway platform with no money and no ticket.
He witnesses people looting shops after a riot breaks out.
He is asked to lie in order to protect his friend from punishment.
He sees a wild animal approach his camp at night.
He is taking an examination when the hall catches fire.
His team loses an important match because of his mistake.
He is asked to leave behind his injured teammate during a trek.
He receives an anonymous letter threatening his family.
He has to arrange a marriage for his younger sister with very limited means.
He is alone on a boat when a storm damages the mast.
He is the first to reach a village where a house has collapsed.
He is asked to work overtime while his child is ill.
He is asked to report on his own colleagues.
He is caught in a crowd when a fire breaks out in a market.
He is asked to reverse a decision he knows was correct.
He is stopped by a mob while driving an ambulance.
He must decide whether to report his friend for breaking a rule.
He is posted in a desolate area with no contact for months.
He is asked to take responsibility for a task that has already failed.
He sees a man about to be attacked by a crowd.
He loses his way while trekking and his water is finished.
He finds that the food served to his men is unfit to eat.
He is asked to guide a foreign delegation with no preparation.
He sees two children playing on a railway track.
He is told he must board a train that is about to leave from another platform.
He is asked to resign for a mistake his whole team made.
He has to choose between saving a drowning man and his own belongings.
He is overcome by fumes while rescuing people from a fire.
He is asked to break a promise in order to keep someone safe.
He finds a ticking parcel in a public place.
He is asked to accompany a patient suffering from a contagious disease.
His friend's wedding clashes with an important examination.
He is asked to give up his seat to a pregnant woman on a long journey.
He notices that a bridge he must cross is cracking.
He is asked to lead men who will not obey his orders.
He sees a person having a seizure in a public place.
He is offered money to keep quiet about a crime.
He must cross a flooded road to reach the polling booth on time.
He is asked to give up his own oxygen mask during a flight emergency.
He is the only one who can drive during a night emergency.
He suspects that a colleague is leaking information to outsiders.
He has to choose between his duty and his friendship.
He is asked to take a decision that will upset everyone around him.
